minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued most hearings to Feb 5, wanted a replanting plan for 90 Hemlock and a remedy for the illegal paving.
minutes.summary: The Commission heard several wetlands hearings and continued most of them: 72 and 90 Hemlock Dr, an earth removal at 1325 Mass Ave, the sunset Lane culverts and a retaining wall. It approved a determination letting a 54 Pine Acres owner maintain her 12-foot driveway, and authorized a capped spend for a tax bill insert. Members also debated how to remedy illegal paving at a lake access lot and raised concerns about a new dual online and paper permitting process.

Continue the 90 Hemlock Dr notice of intent hearing to February 5th

Issue a negative determination allowing the 54 Pine Acres driveway to be maintained at 12 feet in perpetuity
Continue the Sunset Lane and Northfield Road culvert hearing to February 19th
Continue the retaining wall hearing to March 5th
Continue the illegal paving enforcement item to February 5th
Authorize an amount not to exceed $500 for the tri-fold insert in the tax bill
Approve the minutes of the December 18th meeting

budget_items.what_was_said: Printing the tri-fold for the tax bill costs a small per-copy amount, with an estimate of roughly the quoted total. A not-to-exceed cap was proposed, to come from the existing budget.
A member objected that applicants pay an extra electronic filing fee and also pay separate state and local fees.

transfers.description: Funds for the tax bill insert to come from the existing budget

decisions.decision: The 72 Hemlock owner is to bring a marked-up replanting plan by the week before Feb 5 so it can be approved as a field change.
90 Hemlock applicants to prepare a tree removal and replanting plan, with a site walk before the next meeting.
1325 Mass Ave plan to add notes on basin timing before phase four, impervious area, and a maintenance and annual reporting plan.
Retaining wall applicant to get a final continuance; if she does not respond, leave to withdraw may follow.
Agent to consult town counsel on the paving violation and the lake access lot before the commission decides remediation.
Agent to prepare a description of the application process for applicants.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the 90 Hemlock Dr septic and tree removal hearing to February 5 and asked for a tree removal and replanting plan and a site walk.
It continued the 1325 Mass Ave earth removal hearing to February 5, with the plan to add notes on basin timing, impervious area and maintenance and reporting.
It issued a negative determination allowing the 54 Pine Acres driveway to be maintained at its current width.
It continued the illegal paving item at the lake access lot to February 5; the agent is to consult town counsel before the Commission decides on remediation.
It authorized an amount not to exceed a set cap for printing a tri-fold insert in the tax bill, to come from the existing budget.

why_it_matters: Several wetlands projects, including a septic replacement, an earth removal and the lake access paving, stay undecided until at least February 5, so neighbors and applicants have another hearing to attend.
The tax bill insert is a small spend from the existing budget, and applicants face electronic filing fees on top of state and local permit fees under the new permitting process.
watch_next: February 5 hearings on 72 and 90 Hemlock Dr, 1325 Mass Ave and the lake access lot paving, after the agent consults town counsel.
Later continuances: the Sunset Lane and Northfield Road culverts on February 19 and the retaining wall on March 5.
